readme:
# p-Hacking and Publication Bias in Design-Based Causal Studies in Information Systems — Replication Package

[REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED]

Data and code that reproduce every table and figure in:

> Mike Nguyen and Minh Nguyen (2026). p-Hacking and Publication Bias in Design-Based Causal Studies in Information Systems. *Information Systems Research.* <https://doi.org/10.1287/isre.2024.1365>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What this is

A metascience audit of causal inference in information systems research. We hand-coded 7,516 hypothesis tests from 558 articles by 1,087 authors, published 2000–2023 in the seven leading IS journals (ISR, MISQ, JMIS, Management Science, JAIS, ISJ, JIT), covering five design-based identification strategies (e.g., difference-in-differences (DID), instrumental variables (IV), randomized controlled trials (RCT), regression discontinuity (RD), and synthetic control (SC)) and tested whether the published distribution of test statistics shows the fingerprints of p-hacking and publication bias.

Headline findings, all reproducible from this package:

| Finding | Value |
|----|----|
| Excess mass of test statistics just above *z* = 1.96 | DID, IV, RCT, but not RD or SC |
| Observed vs. expected discovery rate (*z*-curve) | ODR 0.58 vs. EDR 0.20, a gap of 0.38 |
| Expected replication rate for IS causal studies | 65% (95% CI 61–71%) |
| IS IV papers that are just-identified | 96.65% |
| IV papers reporting first-stage *F* \< 142.6 | 68% |
| Significant IV results reversed by the tF correction | 25% |
| Estimated share of reported *z*-statistics consistent with a null | π̂₀ ≈ 0.83 |
| Local false discovery rate at *z* = 1.96 | 0.31 (DID), 0.47 (IV), 0.23 (RCT) |

The package ships the cleaned analysis files. No data collection, scraping or hand-coding is re-run.

Keywords: p-hacking · publication bias · causal inference · information systems · metascience · research transparency · reproducibility · z-curve · caliper test · randomization test · local false discovery rate · weak instruments · tF correction · difference-in-differences · instrumental variables · regression discontinuity · synthetic control · R · Quarto · renv

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Quick start

``` r
# 1. restore the exact package versions used for the paper
Rscript -e 'renv::restore()'

# 2. reproduce everything
Rscript run_all.R
```

Output lands in `output/`. A full run takes roughly 4-6 minutes with the cached intermediates in `data/precomputed/` (the default).

If you prefer not to use `renv`, `Rscript code/install_dependencies.R` installs the same packages at whatever versions are current — see Environment below for the two places where that matters.

To work interactively, open `replication.Rproj` and render whichever document in `code/` covers the section you are interested in.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Contents

```

├── run_all.R                     master script -- renders all six documents
├── renv.lock                     exact package versions (see Environment)
├── CITATION.cff                  machine-readable citation metadata
├── code/
│   ├── 00_setup.R                paths, packages, seed, export helpers
│   ├── install_dependencies.R    unpinned fallback installer
│   ├── 01_descriptives.qmd       Sections 3-4    Table 2, Figures 1-2
│   ├── 02_zcurve_and_randomization.qmd
│   │                             Sections 5.1-5.2
│   │                             Tables 4, 5; Figures 3-4
│   ├── 03_caliper.qmd            Section 5.3     Table 6
│   ├── 04_caliper_robustness.qmd Appendix C.3    caliper robustness
│   ├── 05_mechanisms.qmd         Sections 5.4    Tables 7-11; Figures 5-6
│   ├── 06_fdr_and_remedies.qmd   Section 5.5     Table 12
│   ├── robust/
│   │   └── caliper_models.R      the caliper-test logit specifications
│   └── third_party/              code by other authors
├── data/
│   ├── articles.rds              one row per reported test
│   ├── articles_author_lv.rds    the same tests x author
│   ├── brodeur2020_A11.xlsx      Brodeur et al. (2020) Table A11
│   └── precomputed/              cached results of the long-running steps
├── docs/
│   ├── CODEBOOK.md               every variable and its definition
│   └── OUTPUT_MAP.md             which file produces which numbered exhibit
├── output/                       everything the code writes

```

Each analysis document is self-contained: it loads `00_setup.R`, the third-party code and the data, then writes its own outputs. Render them in any order, or open just the one covering the section of the paper you care about. `docs/OUTPUT_MAP.md` maps every generated file to its table or figure number.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## The data

`data/articles.rds` is the analysis file: one row per statistical test hand-coded from a published article.

`data/articles_author_lv.rds` expands the same tests to one row per test × author.

Both files carry only the columns the analysis uses, plus the bibliographic keys (`article`, `doi`, `title`, `journal`, `year`, `method`, `table`) needed to trace a coded test back to its source article. Intermediate columns from the construction pipeline, unused IV diagnostics, Crossref metadata and abstracts have been dropped. Every retained column is unchanged.

`docs/CODEBOOK.md` documents every variable.

Author identifiers. Author names are not distributed. `full_name` was replaced by the surrogate key `author_id` (which is all the analysis uses it for, counting distinct authors and de-duplicating author rows).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Environment

The paper's tables carry generation stamps (`% latex table generated in R 4.4.3 by xtable 1.8-4 package`, dated 24–27 September 2025). `renv.lock` therefore pins R 4.4.3 and the CRAN snapshot of 2025-09-27; `xtable` 1.8-4 was the current CRAN version until February 2026, which confirms the snapshot date.

Two dependencies matter for exact reproduction:

- `marginaleffects` must be 0.26.0 or older. From 0.28 onwards it refuses to compute standard errors for a `fixest` model with fixed effects, so Table 6 cannot be produced at all.
- `fixest` 0.12.1, 0.13.2 and 0.14.1 all give the same estimates here; the pinned version is 0.13.2.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Long-running steps

The pooled z-curve (500 bootstrap replications), the z-curve fitted separately by method × year and journal × year, and the Elliott, Kudrin and Wuthrich (2022) test battery take hours. Their results are cached in `data/precomputed/` and the chunks that produce them are switched off by default.

To regenerate them, set `RUN_EXPENSIVE <- TRUE` in the setup chunk of `code/02_zcurve_and_randomization.qmd`. Fresh results are written to `output/derived/` and read back from there, so the shipped cache is never overwritten.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Third-party code and data

This package redistributes code and data written by others. Each file keeps its original author header. If you use any of it, cite the original source.

## `code/third_party/pcurve_app.R`

The p-curve app, version 4.052 (2017-03-17), written by Uri Simonsohn. Obtained from <http://p-curve.com/app4/>. Used unmodified to produce the p-curve figures and the binomial / Stouffer tests.

> Simonsohn, U., Nelson, L. D., & Simmons, J. P. (2014). P-curve: A key to the file-drawer. *Journal of Experimental Psychology: General*, 143(2), 534-547.

## `code/third_party/elliott_tests.R`

Test suite from the replication package for "Detecting p-hacking", by Graham Elliott, Nikolay Kudrin and Kaspar Wuthrich. Used unmodified; provides the binomial, discontinuity, LCM, Cox-Shi and Fisher tests. The authors distribute it "as is" without warranty.

> Elliott, G., Kudrin, N., & Wuthrich, K. (2022). Detecting p-hacking. *Econometrica*, 90(2), 887-906.

## `data/brodeur2020_A11.xlsx`

Appendix Table A11 from Brodeur, Cook and Heyes (2020), transcribed for the cross-discipline comparison in the paper.

> Brodeur, A., Cook, N., & Heyes, A. (2020). Methods matter: p-hacking and publication bias in causal analysis in economics. *American Economic Review*, 110(11), 3634-3660.

## Helper functions

`ama_theme()`, `nice_tab()`, `export_tab()` and `export_fig()` in `code/00_setup.R` are inlined from the authors' own `causalverse` package (<https://github.com/mikenguyen13/causalverse>) so that this package installs entirely from CRAN and Bioconductor. `export_tab()` and `export_fig()` drop the date-stamped `archive/` copies the originals wrote, which makes repeated runs byte-comparable; behaviour is otherwise identical.
